reasons.text: Claimed tonnage in the busiest month would need 256% of the plant's connected load running non-stop (above 100% is physically impossible)
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 92% of months
Electricity bought is only 0.21x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (63 kWh/t against at least 300)
45% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Uploaded plant photos are near-duplicates of photos registered by 1 other plant(s)
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.31x the cost floor)

inspection_checklist: Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Compare the plant against the entities sharing its identifiers (bank, address, director, photos); consider a joint inspection.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
